candidates.name: Myocardial Infarction
support_spans: ECG showed abnormal Q wave and ST-segment elevation with terminal T-wave inversion in leads II, III, and aVF
Mildly elevated cardiac enzymes (creatine kinase: 237 U/L)
High-sensitivity troponin I: 3348 pg/mL
candidates.why: The patient presented with chest pain, ECG changes, and elevated cardiac enzymes, which are all consistent with myocardial infarction.

candidates.name: Inferior Wall Myocardial Infarction with Aneurysm Formation
support_spans: inferior-posterior left ventricular wall akinesis with small pericardial effusion
Large aneurysm formation with myocardial defect (3 cm diameter) in inferior wall
candidates.why: The patient's ECG and echocardiography results show evidence of inferior wall myocardial infarction, and the follow-up tests reveal aneurysm formation in the same area.

candidates.name: Acute Coronary Syndrome
support_spans: intermittent chest pain over 10 days and heavy chest pain lasting for 3 hours
Thrombotic obstruction in right coronary artery
Significant stenosis in left anterior descending and circumflex arteries
candidates.why: The patient's symptoms and coronary angiography results are consistent with acute coronary syndrome, which encompasses a range of conditions including myocardial infarction and unstable angina.

candidates.name: Myocardial Infarction with Ventricular Aneurysm Formation
